title: 9.1 Sample Spaces and Probability

icans: I can list the outcomes in a sample space and count them.
I can find theoretical probabilities and the probability of a complement.
I can find geometric and experimental probabilities.

vocab: an action or trial with __________ results
a _____________ of one or more outcomes
a number from 0 (_____________) to 1 (certain) that measures how likely an event is
(number of ____________ outcomes) ÷ (total number of outcomes), when outcomes are equally likely
all ___________ not in A;  P(not A) = 1 − P(A)
a probability found from __________ or areas

blocks.sec: Part 1 · Notes and examples (fill in each note, then work the example)

notes: Reading a probability: Probability 0 means _______________; probability 1 means _______________.

blocks.stem: You flip a coin and spin a spinner with three equal sections: red, blue, and green. List the sample space. How many outcomes are there?

You guess on three true-false questions. Find the probability that you get
a.  all three correct.        b.  exactly two correct.
A dart lands at a random point on a square board 20 inches on a side. A circle with a radius of 5 inches is in the center. What is the probability that the dart lands in the circle?
A spinner has 8 equal sections numbered 1 to 8. Find P(a number greater than 5) and P(a number not greater than 5).

tickets.stem: You roll a die and flip a coin. How many outcomes are in the sample space?
You roll a die. What is the probability of rolling a number less than 3?
